item.title: Hurricane Isaias Slams Florida Panhandle
item.description: AccuWeather Correspondent Bill Wadell joins hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend from Pensacola Beach, Florida, where Hurricane Isaias made landfall as a Category 2 storm, bringing damaging winds, flooding and widespread power outages across the Gulf Coast. Wadell says the storm has weakened as it moves inland, but downed power lines, debris and continued flooding remain concerns as crews begin restoring electricity and assessing the damage. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump's Russian Diesel Deal Draws Ukraine Criticism
item.description: Atlantic National Security Staff Writer Nancy Youssef tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump's agreement to import Russian diesel could provide limited relief from high fuel prices while potentially increasing Moscow's revenue as it continues its war in Ukraine. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Youssef also discusses Pentagon planning for possible new strikes against Iran and the challenges facing indirect negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz and a potential ceasefire. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why This Canadian Community Is Betting on Coal Again
item.description: A proposed metallurgical coal mine in Alberta’s Crowsnest Pass is reviving an old industry at a time when Canada is looking for new trade relationships beyond the United States. Northback Holdings says Grassy Mountain could supply steelmaking coal to customers in Europe and Asia while bringing jobs and investment back to a community that lost much of its mining economy. But opponents, including musician and activist Corb Lund, warn that the project could threaten water quality and surrounding communities. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Poland Central Bank Faces Meeting Hurdles Without Glapinski: PAP
item.description: The potential suspension of Polish central bank governor Adam Glapinski could make it difficult to convene meetings of the rate-setting panel, a policymaker said, as an “unprecedented” legal challenge raises questions about the institution’s leadership.
item.dc:creator: Zosia Wanat

item.title: Rich Countries Are Now on Front Lines as World’s Risk Map Shifts
item.description: Typically called into action when poor countries get mired in debt, the International Monetary Fund will be confronted this week with mounting signs of trouble in the wealthiest ones.
item.dc:creator: Jorgelina do Rosario

item.title: China Passenger Vehicle Retail Sales Drop 24% in September
item.description: China’s passenger vehicle retail sales fell 24% in September from a year earlier to 1.702 million units, while new-energy vehicle sales declined 12% to 1.141 million units, according to data released by the China Passenger Car Association.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Banking Stock Swoon in Europe Is a Sign of Caution, Not Panic
item.description: A selloff in banking stocks is rarely comforting. But after three years of strong gains, the latest pullback in European lenders looks more like a reset than a crash.
item.dc:creator: Macarena Muñoz and Julien Ponthus

item.title: China Targets AI-Linked Jobs With New Employment Initiative
item.description: China will launch an employment initiative aimed at adapting skills to the development of artificial intelligence, human-resources officials said at a State Council Information Office briefing on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Taiwan’s Lai Urges Democracies to Unite After Trump-Xi Talks
item.description: Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te called on democracies in the region to unite against threats to stability, as the island faces pressure from Beijing and concerns that US President Donald Trump’s rapprochement with China could come at Taiwan’s expense.
item.dc:creator: Yian Lee

item.title: India Detains Student Leaders in Major Crackdown on Protests
item.description: Indian authorities detained leaders of a youth-led protest movement and their allies on Saturday and imposed sweeping restrictions in central Delhi to stop crowds from gathering for a planned demonstration against a contentious revision of voter rolls.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Roy, Atul Dev and Asmi Bhatia

item.title: India Announces Emergency Steps to Support Plunging Currency
item.description: India’s central bank rolled out a series of measures to support the sliding rupee in its strongest action since the country’s currency crisis in 2013.
item.dc:creator: Subhadip Sircar, Pratigya Vajpayee and Bhaskar Dutta

item.title: Thai Bourse Revises Short-Selling, High-Frequency Trading Rules
item.description: Thailand’s stock exchange will roll out revised rules from Nov. 16, including changes to short-selling and high-frequency trading, as it seeks to improve market stability, liquidity and investor confidence, according to a filing.
item.dc:creator: Satid Sutipanya

item.title: Australia Says Doesn’t Need Russian Fuel After Trump Diesel Move
item.description: Australia has no need to buy fuel from Russia and said that purchases from there will remain barred so that the country doesn’t benefit from the invasion of Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Garfield Reynolds

item.title: Safari Park Plan Sparks Fresh Wave of Resident Angst in Vietnam
item.description: In the rolling hills of Ba Vi mountain range just outside Hanoi, the planned construction of a new safari park is causing consternation among residents and has sparked a backlash against the development of an area of great natural beauty.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Stevens and Cao Ban

item.title: Trump Says Putin to Supply US With Diesel
item.description: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are ProShares' Alessio De Longis, Flexport's Ryan Peterson, Raymond James & Associates' Inc Savanthi Syth, Council of Economic Advisers former Chair Jared Bernstein, Wealth Enhancement Group's Ayako Yoshioka, CFRA's Ken Leon, Atomic Machines CEO Jeff Holden, MoffettNathanson's Nick Del Deo. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wall Street Week | Michigan Manufacturing, AI Debt Investments, Baby Bonds, Canadian Coal Fight
item.description: This week, Ford, JPMorgan and the state of Michigan team up to help domestic manufacturers turn new technology into factories and supply chains. And, hyperscalers and data centers are borrowing hundreds of billions of dollars to finance AI infrastructure, transforming the corporate bond market. Plus, can baby bonds actually narrow America’s wealth gap? Later, Alberta’s Grassy Mountain project has become a test of whether Canada can expand resource exports without reigniting old environmental conflicts. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Flexport CEO on Oil Tanker Costs, Diesel Prices
item.description: Flexport CEO, Chairman, and Founder, discusses oil tanker costs, diesel prices and AI in an interview with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Atomic Machines CEO on Developing 'Micro-Machines'
item.description: Atomic Machines CEO Jeffrey Holden discusses a new kind of factory that takes digital code and produces 'micro-machines.' He says the technology is being developed to support a broader range of 'micro-machines.' He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bambusa Therapeutics Files for IPO to Fund Eczema Drug Trials
item.description: Bambusa Therapeutics Inc. filed for a initial public offering to help fund trials of its drugs to treat eczema and other inflammation disorders.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Hughes

item.title: Gold Clinches Weekly Gain on Growing Bullish ETF, Energy Signs
item.description: Gold advanced, notching a weekly gain amid rising demand for bullion-backed exchange traded funds and signs that inflation may ease.
item.dc:creator: Sybilla Gross
